Hi, Thanks for writing in. Endometriosis is a condition where the tissue that normally lines the inside of your uterus (endometrium) grows outside the uterus. This tissue continues to act like normal endometrial tissue and responds to the hormones produced by your ovaries. The tissue may grow on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, bladder, intestines, or other organs. It can also grow in the abdominal cavity. The most common symptom of endometriosis is pelvic pain, which usually occurs before menstruation and decreases after menstruation ends. Pain during intercourse is also common. Other symptoms include painful bowel movements, painful urination, fatigue, and heavy menstrual bleeding. Treatment options for endometriosis include medicines and surgery. Medicines are used to relieve pain and prevent new growths. Surgery is used to remove the growths. Laparoscopic surgery is the most common type of surgery for endometriosis. Laparoscopy is a surgical procedure in which a thin, lighted tube called a laparoscope is inserted through a small cut in the abdomen. The laparoscope has a camera attached to it, and it is used to view the pelvic organs on a video screen. The surgeon can then use tools inserted through additional small cuts to remove or destroy growths. Laparoscopic surgery is usually done on an outpatient basis, which means that you go home the same day. Laparoscopic surgery is less invasive than open surgery and has fewer complications. It also allows the surgeon to see the entire pelvis and to treat many problems at the same time. Laparoscopic surgery is not always successful in treating endometriosis. If the growths cannot be removed completely, they may return. In some cases, the surgeon may need to do more than one laparoscopic surgery to remove all of the growths. Laparoscopic surgery is not recommended if you are trying to become pregnant. Laparoscopic surgery is also not recommended if you have severe endometriosis that involves large areas of your pelvis. In this case, the surgeon may need to do open surgery. Open surgery is a major operation that requires a larger incision. It is usually done if laparoscopic surgery is not successful or if you have severe endometriosis. I hope this helps.

Malrotation with volvulus is characterized by a lack of normal rotation of the stomach and intestines during fetal development.
